idea: Fix our on-call rotation: whoever is on call must answer pages within 5 minutes, 24/7 including overnight, with no real backup plan when someone is sick or traveling.
source: HISTORICAL, SUPERSEDED -- produced by slicer_live.py (since deleted) against tools/gap-library.yaml (since retired, folded into tools/world-knowledge.yaml). No idea-specific piece text authored by Claude; that much still holds. But the piece texts below are the pre-polarity-fix wording (problem statements, not requirement statements -- see world-knowledge.yaml's gap_categories comment) and the selection used a single-model 0.6 threshold rather than the current multi-model top-k. Kept as a historical record, not a current artifact. The current live mechanism is foundry/layered_walk.py; its output lands in foundry/runs/<idea>-layered-walk.jsonl, rendered by foundry/report.py, not written back to problems/*.json.

pieces.text: Solving this requires people to change an existing habit or behavior, not just get a new tool.
Solving this requires a clear decision-making or escalation path that doesn't already exist.
Solving this requires something to be distributed or shared fairly across multiple people, not concentrated on one or a few.
Solving this requires someone to be able to see or track status that isn't currently visible.
Solving this requires documenting or transferring knowledge that currently exists only in specific people's heads.
Solving this is constrained by a policy, legal, or contractual rule that must not be violated.
Solving this depends on having enough budget, headcount, or resource, not just the right design.
Solving this depends on people trusting a new mechanism enough to actually rely on it, not just it existing.
The current situation depends on one person or thing with no backup, creating a single point of failure.
It's currently unclear how to measure whether this problem is actually getting better or worse.
